content.text:
Summary of what was implemented: ## 1. API route: `/api/user/preferences` API route at `app/api/user/preferences/route.ts` that returns user preferences. For now it returns mock data that changes per request (theme, language, notifications, `updatedAt`). ## 2. UserDashboard component `UserDashboard` is implemented as an async Server Component that: - Fetches from `/api/user/preferences` using `cache: 'no-store'` so each request gets fresh data - Builds the base URL from `headers()` so it works in dev and production - Renders theme, language, notifications, and last updated time ```18:45:app/UserDashboard.tsx export default async function UserDashboard() { const preferences = await getUserPreferences(); return (

User Dashboard

Your Preferences

  • Theme: {preferences.theme}
  • Language: {preferences.language}
  • Notifications: {preferences.notifications ? 'Enabled' : 'Disabled'}
  • Last updated: {preferences.updatedAt}
); } ``` This matches the existing pattern in `page.tsx` (async Server Components with `fetch`), but uses `cache: 'no-store'` so the preferences are not cached and are re-fetched on every request. The build ran successfully, and the page is marked as dynamic (`ƒ`), so it is server-rendered on each request.
